name: Ausra Fridrikas

She won U-20 World Championships in 1985 (age 18) and 1987 (age 20) before becoming senior world champion in 1990.

family_context_summary: Born in Varėna, Lithuania (then Soviet Union); family background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Soviet sports system, early talent identification, top club access, national team pipeline
evidence_summary: Fridrikas started handball relatively late at age 15 but her talent was quickly identified, and she was playing senior competitions by 16. The Soviet sports pipeline moved her to top club Eglė Vilnius at 17, and she won U-20 World Championships at 18 and 20 before claiming senior World Championship gold at 23. No family background information was found in reviewed sources. Her rapid rise from beginner to world champion in 8 years suggests exceptional physical talent combined with the elite Soviet gymnastics-style pipeline for handball.

name: Horacio Pagani
milestone_by_age_26: Designed and built his first Formula 3 racing car by age 20 in Argentina, establishing himself as a self-taught automotive engineer and fabricator.
early_history_summary: Born in rural Casilda, Argentina to an Italian immigrant baker father and artist mother, Pagani began making balsa wood car models at age 10-11 and built minibikes at 14. He enrolled in industrial design at university at 18 but left to open his own workshop, where he designed and built a complete Formula 3 racer by age 20.
family_context_summary: Born to Luca Pagani, an Italian immigrant baker, and Maria Pagani, an artist; modest working-class family in rural Argentina with no automotive industry connections.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a baker from Italy; mother was an artist. Neither had automotive industry expertise, though both were makers who worked with their hands.
primary_early_advantage_tags: self-taught fabrication, early workshop access, childhood obsession with cars, friend collaborator, rural isolation as catalyst
evidence_summary: Pagani grew up in a small rural town far from any automotive industry, the son of a baker and an artist with no automotive connections. He was obsessively focused on cars from childhood, making balsa wood models at 10 and building minibikes at 14. He opened his own workshop as a teenager and designed and built a complete Formula 3 racer by age 20, an extraordinary feat of self-taught engineering. His isolation from the automotive world may have driven his determination to eventually move to Italy. Sources differ slightly on whether the racer was built at age 20 (Wikipedia) or age 21-22 (Pagani's own recollection in interviews), but all agree it was well before age 26.
starting_point: Born in 1955 in Casilda, a small rural town in Santa Fe, Argentina, to an Italian immigrant baker father and an artist mother; modest working-class family with no automotive industry connections.
current_position: Founder, Chairman, and Chief Designer of Pagani Automobili S.p.A. in Modena, Italy; net worth estimated in hundreds of millions of dollars; globally recognized hypercar manufacturer.

trajectory.event: Designed and built his first Formula 3 racing car in Argentina, establishing himself as a self-taught automotive engineer.

Launched the Pagani Zonda, the first hypercar bearing his name, establishing Pagani Automobili as a premier brand.

name: Jan Švankmajer
milestone_by_age_26: Founded the puppet theater Divadlo masek (Theatre of Masks) in Prague in 1960 at age 26, establishing himself as an independent theater artist before transitioning to filmmaking.
early_history_summary: Švankmajer received a puppet theater at age nine, which profoundly shaped his artistic direction. He studied scenography at the Higher School of Art Industry (1950-1954) and then puppetry at the Academy of Performing Arts (DAMU) in Prague (1954-1958), before working in a puppet theater in Liberec and founding his own Theatre of Masks in Prague around 1960.
primary_leverage_engine: Early specialization in puppetry and visual arts
family_context_summary: Born in Prague to a window dresser father and seamstress mother; received a home puppet theater at age nine that shaped his artistic direction.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a window dresser and mother a seamstress; not directly in the arts but tangentially related to visual presentation and craftsmanship.
primary_early_advantage_tags: DAMU Academy, Prague arts scene, puppet theater tradition, childhood puppet theater, wife as creative partner
evidence_summary: Švankmajer's artistic path was set by a childhood gift of a puppet theater at age nine. He received formal training at two elite Prague institutions: the Higher School of Art Industry (scenography, 1950-1954) and the Academy of Performing Arts DAMU (puppetry, 1954-1958). After working in a puppet theater in Liberec, he founded his own Theatre of Masks in Prague around 1960 at age 26. His parents were a window dresser and seamstress, not wealthy but connected to visual crafts. His later fame as a filmmaker came after age 30 with his first film in 1964, but the theater founding at 26 represents a material milestone in his artistic career.
starting_point: Born in 1934 in Prague, Czechoslovakia to a window dresser father and seamstress mother; received a puppet theater as a Christmas gift at age nine that profoundly shaped his artistic direction.
current_position: Retired filmmaker and artist living in Prague; last film 'Alchemical Furnace' released in 2018 at age 84; remains a leading figure in Czech surrealism.

trajectory.event: Founded the puppet theater Divadlo masek (Theatre of Masks) in Prague, marking his emergence as an independent theater artist.

name: André Noyelle
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic gold medals in both the individual road race and team road race at the 1952 Summer Olympics in Helsinki at age 20, also adding World Championship silver in the amateur road race the same year.
early_history_summary: Born in Ypres, Belgium, Noyelle had a breakthrough year in 1952 when he won double Olympic gold in Helsinki and World Championship silver in Luxembourg, all at age 20. He turned professional the following year with Alcyon-Dunlop and raced professionally through 1966, though he never reached the same heights as a professional.
primary_leverage_engine: Physical talent and Belgian cycling tradition
family_context_summary: Born in Ypres, West Flanders, Belgium; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Belgian cycling tradition, Olympic team selection, teammate support, exceptional physical talent
evidence_summary: Noyelle won double Olympic gold at the 1952 Helsinki Games at age 20, a remarkable achievement that made him the only Belgian cyclist to win the Olympic road race title for 64 years. Belgium's deep cycling tradition and competitive structure provided the ecosystem for his development. He also won World Championship silver the same year. No family background information was found in reviewed sources. His professional career was solid but unspectacular, suggesting his Olympic peak was the highlight of his career.
starting_point: Born in 1931 in Ypres, West Flanders, Belgium; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Died in 2003 at age 71 in Poperinge, Belgium; final role: retired professional cyclist who ran a bicycle shop and a pub called Café Helsinki in his native Ypres.

name: José Manuel Fuente
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1972 Vuelta a España overall classification at age 26, having already won a stage and the King of the Mountains classification at the 1971 Giro d'Italia at age 25.
early_history_summary: Born in Limanes, Asturias, Spain, Fuente came to cycling through a friend and trained as an amateur while working in a metal fabrication shop. Military service and conflicts with team directors delayed his professional debut until 1970 at age 24, but he immediately won the best first-year professional jersey at the Vuelta a España and quickly became one of the greatest climbers of his generation.
family_context_summary: Born in Limanes, Asturias, Spain; from a working-class background, worked in a metal fabrication shop while training as an amateur cyclist. Faced family opposition when he left a steady job to pursue cycling.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father and grandfather shared the nickname 'El Tarangu,' an Asturian word for a man of strength and character, but no direct cycling domain advantage documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: working-class background, metal shop work, military service delay, family opposition, early amateur mentors, Asturian cycling culture
evidence_summary: Fuente's path to professional cycling was delayed by having to work in a metal fabrication shop, military service, and conflicts with team directors. He turned professional late at age 24 in 1970 but immediately made an impact, winning the best first-year professional jersey at the Vuelta. By age 26, he had won the Vuelta a España overall and the Giro d'Italia KOM classification, establishing himself as one of the greatest climbers of his generation and a rival to Eddy Merckx. His working-class background and the obstacles he overcame suggest constraint-driven self-creation rather than inherited advantage.

current_position: Died in 1996 at age 50 in Oviedo, Spain after a long battle with kidney disease; final role: former professional cyclist and cycle shop owner.

name: Canelo Álvarez
milestone_by_age_26: Won the WBC light middleweight (super welterweight) championship at age 20 in March 2011, becoming the youngest super-welterweight champion in boxing history, after turning professional at age 15.
early_history_summary: Born on the outskirts of Guadalajara, Mexico to a large family of modest means, Álvarez was inspired to box by his older brother Rigoberto. He began training at the Reynoso gym and turned professional at age 15 in October 2005. By age 20, he had compiled a 36-0-1 record and won the WBC light middleweight title, becoming the youngest super-welterweight champion ever.
primary_leverage_engine: Physical talent and early professional specialization
family_context_summary: Youngest of seven sons and one daughter born to Santos Álvarez and Ana Maria Barragán; family ran a paleta (fruit popsicle) business and lived on a farm near Guadalajara. Modest means; children helped sell paletas at markets.
parent_family_domain_summary: Older brother Rigoberto Álvarez was the first in the family to take up boxing and became a former interim WBA light middleweight champion, directly inspiring Canelo's boxing career. Multiple brothers boxed.
primary_early_advantage_tags: older brother boxer inspiration, Reynoso trainers, Mexican boxing culture, early pro debut at 15, exceptional physical talent, modest family background, large boxing family
evidence_summary: Álvarez grew up in a large, modest family near Guadalajara, Mexico, where his older brother Rigoberto inspired him to box. He began training at the Reynoso gym (Chepo and Eddy Reynoso) and turned professional at just 15, accumulating 36 fights by age 20. His exceptional physical talent was evident early — the Reynosos accelerated his pro debut after being impressed by his ability. At 20, he won the WBC light middleweight title, becoming the youngest super-welterweight champion ever. The combination of a boxing family, dedicated trainers, Mexican boxing culture, and extraordinary physical talent drove his early success.
starting_point: Born in 1990 on the outskirts of Guadalajara, Jalisco, Mexico to a large family of modest means; parents ran a paleta (fruit popsicle) business; youngest of eight children with several older brothers who boxed.
current_position: Unified super middleweight world champion and global boxing superstar; estimated net worth approximately $275 million; resides in Sherman Oaks, California.

name: Svetlana Boginskaya
milestone_by_age_26: Won two Olympic gold medals (team and vault) at the 1988 Seoul Olympics at age 15, after becoming a Soviet national team member at 14 and winning a World Championship bronze at the 1987 World Championships.
early_history_summary: Born in Minsk, Belarus, Boginskaya practiced figure skating before switching to gymnastics at age six after seeing Nadia Comăneci. She moved to Moscow at age eight to train full-time at the Round Lake Gymnastics Center under coach Lyubov Miromanova, joined the Soviet national team at 14, and won her first Olympic golds at 15 in Seoul.
primary_leverage_engine: Physical talent and Soviet gymnastics pipeline
family_context_summary: Born in Minsk, Belarusian SSR, Soviet Union; family background not documented in reviewed sources beyond early figure skating and gymnastics training.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Soviet gymnastics system, Round Lake training center, national team at 14, elite coaching, Olympic gold at 15, exceptional physical talent
evidence_summary: Boginskaya's path was defined by the elite Soviet gymnastics pipeline: gymnastics from age six, full-time training at the Round Lake center from age eight under coach Lyubov Miromanova (who served as a surrogate mother), and national team selection at 14. She won Olympic gold at 15, World all-around titles at 16, and swept all five European Championship events at 17. The Soviet gymnastics apparatus — elite facilities, dedicated coaching, intense training — was the dominant early advantage. No family background information was found in reviewed sources. Her extraordinary physical talent was evident in her rapid ascent to Olympic champion by age 15.

name: Rafael Aghayev
milestone_by_age_26: Won his first senior World Championship title in the -70 kg kumite event at the 2006 World Karate Championships in Tampere, Finland at age 21, having already become a junior European Champion in 2002 at age 17.
early_history_summary: Born in Sumgait, Azerbaijan to a professional soccer player father, Aghayev started karate at age seven under coach Rafael Mammadov. He was invited to train at the prestigious Budokan club under Fizuli Musayev and joined the national team at age 12 in 1997. He won his first junior European Championship in 2002 and his first senior world title in 2006 at age 21.
primary_leverage_engine: Physical talent and early karate specialization
family_context_summary: Born in 1985 in Sumgait, Azerbaijan to a professional soccer player father and homemaker mother; grew up in a sports-oriented family with two older brothers competing in judo and boxing.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a professional soccer player who cultivated a love of sports in all three sons. Oldest brother Ruslan trained in judo, second brother Rustam in boxing. No direct karate domain advantage, but a strong athletic family culture.
primary_early_advantage_tags: sports family, early karate at 7, Budokan club, dedicated coaches, national team at 12, exceptional physical talent, junior European champion at 17
evidence_summary: Aghayev grew up in a sports family in Sumgait, Azerbaijan — his father was a professional soccer player and his brothers competed in judo and boxing. He started karate at age seven under Rafael Mammadov, was spotted at a national competition and invited to train at the prestigious Budokan club under Fizuli Musayev, and joined the national team at 12. Senior team coach Hidayat Shabanov trained him for over eight years. He won his first junior European Championship at 17 and his first senior world title at 21, eventually becoming the most decorated karateka in history with five world titles. His father's athletic background and the early identification by coaches were key accelerants.

current_position: Five-time world champion and eleven-time European champion karateka; Karate Combat welterweight champion; widely regarded as the most decorated karateka in history; resides in Azerbaijan.
